daily_brief: European leaders convened virtually on Ukraine's Independence Day to reaffirm military support for Kyiv, with France pledging interceptor missiles critical to air defense as Russian strikes continue to claim civilian lives at their highest rate since the war's early months [RFI, France 24, BBC]. The meeting of the 'Coalition of the Willing,' co-chaired by Macron, Merz, and new UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, comes amid growing concerns over dwindling missile stockpiles across allied nations [The Economist]. Meanwhile, escalating US-Iran tensions dominated economic headlines, with Treasury Secretary Bessent announcing what he termed 'economic D-Day'—a sweeping sanctions offensive—while Iran threatened to shut down Gulf oil exports, further constraining already-reduced Strait of Hormuz traffic [Globe and Mail, The Hindu]. The collapse of US-Canada trade talks triggered fresh 50% tariffs and retaliatory measures, with Prime Minister Carney declaring the two nations 'at war' economically [BBC, Globe and Mail]. In corporate news, Shein launched its long-awaited Hong Kong IPO at a $27 billion valuation, a steep decline from its 2022 peak [BBC, Financial Times, Nikkei Asia].

top_stories.headline: European Allies Rally Behind Ukraine on Independence Day as Air Defense Shortages Mount
bullets: The 'Coalition of the Willing' met virtually on Ukraine's 35th Independence Day, co-chaired by French President Macron, German Chancellor Merz, and new UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham
France announced it will send interceptor missiles to Ukraine following a deadly Russian drone strike on a shopping center in Kryvyi Rih that killed 16 people and injured 130
Civilian death toll in Ukraine in 2026 has reached its highest level since the first months of the invasion, driven by intensified Russian attacks on urban areas

German Foreign Minister Wadephul plans to urge US Secretary of State Rubio to take a more active diplomatic role, noting US involvement has been largely handled by presidential envoys Kushner and Witkoff

top_stories.headline: US Launches 'Economic D-Day' Against Iran as Tehran Threatens Gulf Oil Shutdown
bullets: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced what he called 'the greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary,' targeting Iran's trade partners with sanctions rolling out Monday
Iran responded by threatening to shut down all oil exports from the Gulf if the economic pressure continues
Fewer than 20 commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend, with traffic well below normal levels amid ongoing blockades
Oil prices fell Monday as markets braced for details of the sanctions plan; the US and Iran have not engaged in meaningful peace talks despite weeks without military strikes

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Framed as escalating brinkmanship with focus on diplomatic standstill

sources.framing_note: Emphasized shipping data and economic impacts on global oil markets

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Noted Iran's discovery of new gas reserves amid war-damaged energy infrastructure

top_stories.headline: US-Canada Trade Talks Collapse, Triggering 50% Tariffs and Retaliatory Measures
bullets: Trade negotiations collapsed less than an hour before Friday's deadline after US Commerce Secretary Lutnick pushed for harsher terms than initially agreed
Trump imposed new 50% tariffs on a range of Canadian goods; Prime Minister Carney announced dollar-for-dollar retaliation effective September 8 on steel, dairy, appliances, and electronics
Carney declared the two countries 'at war' economically, while Trump renewed comments about making Canada the '51st state'
Canadian negotiators reported surprise language inserted into final deal text after they believed terms had been agreed on Tuesday

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Balanced coverage of both sides' positions and Trump's annexation rhetoric

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Detailed insider account of negotiation breakdown, emphasizing Lutnick's role and domestic Canadian political pressures

top_stories.headline: Shein Launches Hong Kong IPO at $27 Billion Valuation, Down 70% From Peak
bullets: The fast-fashion giant priced its IPO to raise up to $1.77 billion, with shares to begin trading September 1
Valuation dropped sharply from the $100 billion private market peak in 2022, reflecting weaker sales growth and higher costs
The Hong Kong listing follows failed attempts to go public in the US and London due to regulatory challenges and scrutiny of the company
Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and JP Morgan are backing the offering

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Provided context on company's rise and regulatory challenges

sources.name: Nikkei Asia
sources.framing_note: Emphasized the dramatic valuation decline from peak

top_stories.headline: DRC and M23 Rebels Agree on Peace Roadmap in Swiss-Mediated Talks
bullets: The Democratic Republic of Congo government and M23 rebels agreed on a roadmap setting out sequenced steps and timelines for peace negotiations
Talks held in Switzerland August 17-21 were mediated by the United States, Qatar, Togo, Switzerland, and the African Union Commission
A ceasefire verification mission is set to arrive Monday in Minembwe, South Kivu—the first formal inspection since the November 2025 peace deal
Both parties agreed to establish a mechanism for addressing ceasefire violations and committed to pursue comprehensive peace negotiations

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Noted this as the latest step in a 'cautious' peace process that has not ended fighting
